scope: General/category-agnostic counting for CountScope; evidence distinguishes journal from conference/preprint.

papers.title: SQLNet: Scale-Modulated Query and Localization Network for Few-Shot Class-Agnostic Counting
papers.evidence: Author arXiv v2 explicitly says accepted by TIP; author publication page lists TIP2025; publisher DOI resolves only inconsistently in this environment.
papers.idea: Hierarchical exemplar features, exemplar-size prompts, scale-aware localization and size supervision.
papers.application: Useful mechanism for handling scale diversity and requiring localization as well as count, but the released few-shot model does not remove manual exemplars.
papers.implementationEvidence: Official Readme.md supplies test code/checkpoint; training code is unchecked/not released. ResNet50 backbone; paper uses1280-d exemplar features and1024-d correlation tokens.
papers.macAssessment: No CPU/MPS/CoreML run performed. Architecture may be portable, but sparse/deformable parts must be inspected. Not a turnkey automatic product candidate.

papers.title: Focus for Free in Density-Based Counting
papers.output: density-based count; not a universal category selector
papers.idea: Use existing point labels for count-consistent occlusion augmentation and foreground-mask distillation, suppressing background interference.
papers.application: Transfer as a controlled training ablation for our center/box labels, not as an off-the-shelf colony model. Keep the mask/auxiliary supervision training-only and preserve real test pixels.
papers.implementationEvidence: Publisher links a repository whose README is still the ICCV2019 implementation: Python2.7/TensorFlow1.04/CUDA8 and>=10GB GPU. This is not evidence of a maintained exact2024 reproduction. Paper evaluates crowd datasets; applicability to colonies is a hypothesis.
papers.macAssessment: Do not install that legacy environment into the active venv. Reimplement the limited supervision idea in the present pipeline if justified, and compare per-scale/per-species recall.

papers.title: A Low-Shot Object Counting Network With Iterative Prototype Adaptation
papers.requiresExemplars: Optional; distinct published zero-shot checkpoint and mode require none.
papers.idea: Iteratively adapt object prototypes with image features; few-shot prototypes encode size and appearance, while zero-shot uses learned objectness prototypes.
papers.implementationEvidence: README documents PyTorch1.11/torchvision0.12; evaluate.py hardcodes CUDA/DDP. In zero-shot, models/ope.py bypasses exemplar dimensions and ROIAlign, and models/loca.py can receive bboxes=None. All state must load strictly before bypassing redundant pretrained initialization.
papers.macAssessment: ActualCPU/MPS no-exemplar screen completed with strict author checkpoint loading and unchanged architecture; MPS pilot count differences below0.0001.58-image validation screenMAE22.50 vs cached reference-conditionedFamNet35.04. Negative controls failed strongly. NoCoreML/iPhone acceptance.

papers.title: DAVE - A Detect-and-Verify Paradigm for Low-Shot Counting
papers.requiresExemplars: Zero-shot and text-prompt variants are provided.
papers.idea: Generate high-recall candidates, then verify/cluster appearance features to reject false positives. Zero-shot majority selection can choose the wrong category in mixed scenes; text helps disambiguate.
papers.application: Use the detect-then-verify idea for foreground negatives rather than threshold tuning alone. Check count-vs-box discrepancy and dense-region failures.
papers.implementationEvidence: Official zero-shot demo requires DAVE_0_shot and verification weights, CUDA/DDP; dependencies include sklearn/skimage and optional transformers; Detectron2 is requested for AP evaluation. ROIAlign and non-neural clustering complicate end-to-end CoreML.
papers.macAssessment: A later research candidate, not the first Mac port. No runtime or checkpoint-size verification performed.

papers.title: CountGD: Multi-Modal Open-World Counting
papers.publicationType: top conference, not a journal; not ECCV2024
papers.requiresExemplars: Text-only, exemplars-only or both; text-only avoids drawing boxes.
papers.output: object-center confidence/location; reliable box extents are not the supervised output
papers.idea: Repurpose GroundingDINO for counting, using localization/focal losses and text/visual prompt fusion. A category choice can supply a fixed text prompt while region localization remains automatic.
papers.limitations: The paper notes unusual visual appearances and fine-grained category distinctions can defeat text alone. No guarantee that biological colonies are recognized from a generic word.
papers.implementationEvidence: README checkpoint1.2GB; Swin-B+BERT plus optional SAM ViT-H test-time normalization. Official setup compiles MSDeformAttn with GCC/CUDA; single_image_inference.py has.cuda() calls despite a device arg. Paper reports48GB A6000 training; README full validation6min withoutSAM vs26min withSAM onRTX3090.
papers.macAssessment: Use as a text-only research teacher only after a CPU/fallback-operator port. Do not claim directMPS/CoreML viability or copy Linux/CUDA requirements into the current venv.

papers.title: Generalized-Scale Object Counting with Gradual Query Aggregation
papers.publicationType: peer-reviewed major conference, not a journal; not ICCV2025
papers.idea: Gradually fuse exemplar-conditioned queries across feature scales, retaining both large objects and dense small ones instead of relying on fixed tiling.
papers.application: Useful design evidence for scale-aware whole/crop fusion or multiscale features; cannot be substituted as a no-box model.
papers.implementationEvidence: Paper uses frozen SAM2 Hiera, fixed1024 input, deformable attention and3exemplars; full training200epochs on2A100. Author installer uses Python3.10, CUDA12.6 Torch2.7.1 and compiled Deformable-DETR ops; checked350.8MBdemo checkpoint, not a CoreML asset.
papers.macAssessment: Too much porting for the first small screen. ReducedGPU-memory claims are from A100 measurements and do not establish M5/iPhone memory/latency.

bibliographicCorrections: GeCo is NeurIPS2024; GeCo2 is AAAI2026, not ICCV2025.
SQLNet counting is HCPLab-SYSU/SQLNet; xiaojunxu/SQLNet is an unrelated text-to-SQL project.
IJCV2024 Focus for Free points to an older ICCV2019 codebase; do not claim exact2024 reproduction from its README.

knownDatasetIssuesFromCountGDPaper.issue: Wrong visual exemplars; CountGD paper uses text-only for this image.
Text lego is incorrect for the annotated target; paper changes it to yellow lego stud.

priority.action: Run a frozen58-image class-balanced clean-validation screen for LOCA zero-shot with no GT boxes or text inputs, comparing cached FamNet baseline only as a different-input reference.
priority.why: Most direct low-effort test of the no-manual-exemplar requirement; smaller published checkpoint and no customCUDA op in the zero-shot inference graph.

priority.action: Use DAVE/SQLNet/GeCo2 ideas to test scale-aware context and false-positive verification on validation only, preserving per-size/per-species metrics.
priority.why: Fixed tiling alone can trade large-object recall for small-object recall; MAE can hide FP/FN cancellation.

priority.action: Consider a limited CountGD text-only pilot without SAM after compatibility diagnosis; use target-category prompts and explicit negative/mixed-object cases.
priority.why: Removes drawing exemplars while making target semantics explicit, but is not currently a lightweight on-device drop-in.

evaluationLimits: Previously opened test sets must be treated as regression/development evidence for new decisions.
A paper score on originalFSC147 cannot be compared directly to our cleaned/class-balanced subset as a claimed improvement.
Zero-shot here means no test-time visual exemplars, not no training data and not automatic understanding of the user-intended category.
No new App capability, CoreML/iPhone readiness or successful model improvement is claimed by this literature review.
actionsNotPerformed: No model training in this research lane
